Elena — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary below (short bullets you can paste into your assessment). I've attached a simple diagram and a CSV summary of our retention options.

- Data residency (hosted API): customer requests are routed to compute and storage in the region selected at onboarding (we support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1). By default BrightShore tenant is hosted in the US (us-west-2) per your onboarding flag. PII and prompt/completion payloads are stored on encrypted object storage in that region.
- Default retention: request/response logs and conversational histories are retained by default for 30 days to support troubleshooting, rate-limits, abuse detection, and model quality monitoring.
- Shortening retention: customers can configure tenant-level TTLs down to 0 days (ephemeral) via the Console or API (CreateTenant/UpdateTenantRetention). When TTL=0 we do not persist conversational logs beyond transient cache required for live completion.
- Deletion & backups: deletion requests trigger an immediate eviction from primary storage and application caches. Snapshots/backups are retained per our backup lifecycle (encrypted incremental snapshots retained up to 35 days). When a deletion request is executed we mark the object for purge; the object is removed from the next snapshot cycle and fully purged from backups within 35 days. For tenants requiring faster evidence, we offer an expedited purge process under contract (see SOC2 section excerpt).
- Auditability & evidence: we provide audit logs for deletion requests, tenant retention settings, and the work item id for expedited purges. Logs include timestamp, operator/service account, and related job id.

Attachments: HostedAPI_DataFlow_Diagram.pdf (high level), RetentionPolicy_Summary.csv (options + API endpoints).

If you want a single-paragraph statement for your questionnaire: “Redwood Inference stores hosted-API tenant data in the customer-selected cloud region. Default logs are retained 30 days but tenants can set retention to 0 days to avoid persistence. Deletion requests are processed immediately; objects are evicted from primary stores and purged from backups within our backup lifecycle window (<=35 days) unless an expedited purge is contracted.”

Happy to walk through this on the call — I’ve scheduled 15 minutes after your questionnaire slot.

Elena — quick follow-up from the infra/security side (adding Kim). Answers below: 

- Cross-region replication: we do not replicate tenant workloads to a secondary region by default. For customers that opt into cross-region DR we replicate encrypted snapshots only, not live conversational logs; replication is done using customer-isolated tenant identifiers and all data is encrypted at-rest (AES-256) and in-flight (TLS 1.3). Replicated snapshots remain in the customer’s tenant boundary and access controls mirror the primary region.
- Backup layers & purge: our standard backup cadence: daily incremental snapshots + weekly full backups. Daily incrementals are rolled for up to 35 days; weekly fulls are retained for up to 90 days for operational recovery. When a deletion is issued the object is removed from primary and marked for purge; daily incrementals no longer reference it and will be purged within the 35-day window. Weekly fulls may still contain the object until their next rotation; long-term cold storage is not used for hosted-API tenant backups unless contracted. If BrightShore requires that all backup layers purge within a shorter SLA we can include an expedited purge clause in the contract.
